# Tolerating an optional upstream with the lenient marker

A `?` at the end of a substitution directive makes that one directive resolve to
empty when its source is missing, instead of failing the dispatch. The leniency
is scoped to the marked directive.

## The template

The `optional_upstream` node's only subscription is to a message type nothing
ever sends, so it never runs and the receiver's read of it is a missing source.

```yaml
name: lenient-demo
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: never/sent
    body_schema: {type: object}
nodes:
  - type: trigger
    kind: loop_counter
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 1}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: optional_upstream
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: never/sent
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          label: {type: string, default: present}

  - type: receiver
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: trigger
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: optional_upstream
        type: attribute/label/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          from_optional:
            type: string
            source: "{{nodes.optional_upstream.attribute.label?}}"
          always:
            type: string
            default: "own value"
```

## Without the marker

Drop the `?` from the `from_optional` source and run it.

`optional_upstream` never runs. The receiver settles
`terminal/error/template_resolution_failed`, and the error names the directive
it could not resolve — `nodes.optional_upstream.attribute.label`.

## With the marker

`optional_upstream` still never runs. The receiver dispatches and settles
`terminal/success`.

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/nodes/$RECEIVER_NODE_ID"
```

Its resolved bag reads:

```json
{"from_optional": "", "always": "own value"}
```

The marked property is the empty string; the node's other properties resolved
normally. A template author writes a node that tolerates an optional upstream
without giving up resolution errors everywhere else.
